name: China Pink
lede: China Pink is a deep purplish pink carried by Ridgway's 1912 nomenclature, the ISCC-NBS system and Maerz and Paul, and about 5.8 units from hot pink.

sections.title: Three dictionaries, one pink
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* gives this hue on plate XXVI, hue 67 minutes, tone b [1]. Wikipedia's page on the color cites Plochere as a source and notes the ISCC-NBS 1955 report files the same block, 248, as a deep purplish pink [2][3].

Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary lists the color too, first recorded in 1912 [4]. The ISCC-NBS block 248 is crowded: our library lists ten other names filed in the same block, among them Rosebud (1925), Sweet Briar (1920) and Valencia (1925) [3][4]. The nearest named colors on file are [[light-rosolane-purple]], [[pale-violet-red]], [[cyclamen]] and [[violet-red-perbang]], at 2.7, 3.7, 4.4 and 4.5 ΔE [5].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: ColorHub's archive finds this exact match in only one of 23,781 paintings, Ernst Ludwig Kirchner's 1910 *Two Girls under an Umbrella*, as photographed [6]. A single hit is not a trend; the color is rare in paint even though it is common in dye and dress [6]. It is closer in our data to plain [[pink]] than to the cooler [[orchid]], which leans more purple [6]. The count is a computed color match, not a pigment identification [6].
